## latex_parser::parse_latex

<a id="entry-presentation_rust_native_function_latex_parser_parse_latex"></a>
<a id="placement-placement.rust.native_rust.latex_parser_parse_latex.948e0aaf2f28"></a>
<p class="symi-entry-owner">latex_parser function</p>

```rust signature
pub fn parse_latex(
    source: &str,
    context: &Context,
) -> Result<ExpressionReference, LatexParseError>
```

Parse a LaTeX string in Symi's canonical input dialect — the inverse of `to_latex` and the parser the Symi frontend uses. Returns whichever top-level object the input denotes: an ordinary expression, a `\begin{matrix}…\end{matrix}`, or a geometry figure (`(x, y)` point, segment, polygon, or circle), wrapped in the matching exported class exactly as `parse_serialized_object` does. Coverage spans arithmetic, powers, fractions, roots, the elementary and many special functions, comparisons, integrals (including the bare-`d` differential), Leibniz derivatives (`\frac{d}{dx}` — differentiated eagerly), limits, summations, products, determinants, and actuarial annuities. The resolution is context-aware in a way `parse` is not: a bare `i` is the imaginary unit and a bare `e` is Euler's number unless the letter is a bound index (a summation / product / limit index shadows the constant), and `\mathrm{d}` — or a bare `d` that closes an integral — is the differential operator while a bare `d` elsewhere is an ordinary variable. Raises on syntax errors.

## evaluate_truth

<a id="entry-presentation_rust_api_session_evaluate_truth"></a>
<a id="placement-placement.rust.native_rust.api_session_evaluate_truth.06c39256d903"></a>
<p class="symi-entry-owner">api::Session method</p>

```rust signature
pub fn evaluate_truth(
    &self,
    target: &Expression,
) -> Result<TruthValue, ApiError>
```

Provides the `evaluate_truth` operation on this native type: the exact three-valued verdict of a logical expression, where `unknown` means undecided and never false. Order, equality and sign relations between closed-form real constants — rationals, `pi`, radicals and real algebraic numbers — are decided exactly by rational arithmetic; transcendental, symbolic and provably non-real operands decline.

```rust signature
pub lifted_family_verdict:
```

Stores the decision that the lifted family solves the original equation. It is proved directly when the verifier decides the substituted residual, and otherwise by composition: the reduction identity `Delta(W f(z)) = M R[f](z)` holds for an arbitrary profile, and the reduced family independently verifies `R[g] = 0`, so `Delta(W g(z))` vanishes.

## differential_equations::partial_differential_equations::request::PartialDifferentialEquationGeometricDomain::RealLineEvolution

```rust signature
RealLineEvolution,
```

An evolution chart: the first declared variable is a spatial coordinate ranging over the whole real line and the second is a strictly positive evolution coordinate. Declaring this is what lets a transform route know that the spatial axis is the whole line; inferring it from a variable being spelled `x` would be guessing the geometry from a name.

## differential_equations::partial_differential_equations::request::PartialDifferentialEquationRequestDecline::CompleteFamilyNotEstablished

<a id="entry-presentation_rust_native_variant_differential_equations_partial_differential_equations_request_partialdifferentialequationrequestdecline_completefamilynotestablished"></a>
<a id="placement-placement.rust.native_rust.differential_equations_partial_differential_equations_request_partialdifferentialequationrequestdecline_completefamilynotestablished.ccee2c908358"></a>
<p class="symi-entry-owner">differential_equations::partial_differential_equations::request::PartialDifferentialEquationRequestDecline variant</p>

```rust signature
CompleteFamilyNotEstablished,
```

The request asked for the complete family and the family returned carries no completeness theorem: a verified residual proves membership in the solution set, never coverage of it.

## differential_equations::partial_differential_equations::request::PartialDifferentialEquationRequestDecline::CompletenessHoldsOnlyOnANarrowerSolutionClass

<a id="entry-presentation_rust_native_variant_differential_equations_partial_differential_equations_request_partialdifferentialequationrequestdecline_completenessholdsonlyonanarrowersolutionclass"></a>
<a id="placement-placement.rust.native_rust.differential_equations_partial_differential_equations_request_partialdifferentialequationrequestdecline_completenessholdsonlyonanarrowersolutionclass.ba479a6a260f"></a>
<p class="symi-entry-owner">differential_equations::partial_differential_equations::request::PartialDifferentialEquationRequestDecline variant</p>

```rust signature
CompletenessHoldsOnlyOnANarrowerSolutionClass,
```

A complete family was constructed, but its completeness theorem holds over a narrower class of solutions than the request asked for. This is the honest verdict for the unrestricted heat request: the initial-trace representation is complete among solutions of polynomial growth and the equation has others, so answering the wider question with the narrower theorem would be a false completeness claim rather than a useful approximation.

```rust signature
InitialTraceRepresentationInTheAdmissibleClass,
```

Every solution in the declared admissible class equals the recorded operator applied to its own trace at the initial time. Proof: Tychonoff uniqueness inside the class, together with the operator's kernel identity, mass normalization, and attained initial trace.

<p class="symi-entry-owner">differential_equations::partial_differential_equations::solution_family::PartialDifferentialEquationCompletenessTheorem variant</p>

```rust signature
RegularHarmonicExpansionOnADisk,
```

Every real harmonic function on an open disk has the recorded convergent polar expansion; conversely, every expansion satisfying its coefficient convergence hypothesis is harmonic.

## differential_equations::partial_differential_equations::solution_family::PartialDifferentialEquationCompletenessTheorem::VanishingIteratedDerivativeOnAProductChart

<a id="entry-presentation_rust_native_variant_differential_equations_partial_differential_equations_solution_family_partialdifferentialequationcompletenesstheorem_vanishingiteratedderivativeonaproductchart"></a>
<a id="placement-placement.rust.native_rust.differential_equations_partial_differential_equations_solution_family_partialdifferentialequationcompletenesstheorem_vanishingiteratedderivativeonaproductchart.d6f1dd2c608e"></a>
<p class="symi-entry-owner">differential_equations::partial_differential_equations::solution_family::PartialDifferentialEquationCompletenessTheorem variant</p>

```rust signature
VanishingIteratedDerivativeOnAProductChart,
```

On a connected product of intervals, every solution of an iterated derivative set to zero is the finite sum of coordinate-power multiples of arbitrary functions of the remaining coordinates recorded by the family. Proof: integrate the vanishing derivative once in each of its coordinates, the constant of each integration being an arbitrary function of the coordinates not yet integrated.
